chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from some of our companions, that he
disliked the two kidneys and said: 'But rather these two are the reservoir of the urine.'

key_terms.الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ: The two kidneys — dual form of kulya, the organ that filters blood and produces urine
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked/deemed reprehensible (karaha) — in fiqh terminology, this implies the ruling of makruh (reprehensible), one step below haram
key_terms.مَجْمَعُ الْبَوْلِ: Reservoir of urine — the Imam's explanation for why the kidneys are disliked

ai.seo_question: Are kidneys (kulya) makruh (reprehensible) to eat according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration, the Imam (peace be upon him) expresses his dislike (karahah) for eating the kidneys of an animal, providing a physiological rationale: the kidneys serve as the repository for urine. This establishes a jurisprudential basis for considering the kidneys makruh (reprehensible but not forbidden) to consume. The reasoning reflects the concern for ritual purity and bodily cleanliness that pervades Shia fiqh, as the association of an organ with a najis (ritually impure) substance renders it undesirable even if technically permissible.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin ZIyad, from one of our companions that,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> disliked the two kidneys and said: ‘But rather these two are the reservoir of the urine’.
en.sarwar: 6. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
disliked the kidneys and said that they are the collectors of urine.’”
